title: Networking basics
goal: Check if a service listens and answers, fix "port already in use", read curl results and exit codes, and understand name resolution.
setup: # a tiny website for the local test servers (python3 -m http.server)
# P4: practice copies of /etc/hosts and /etc/resolv.conf (NOT the real files)
printf '%s\n' '127.0.0.1   localhost' '::1         localhost ip6-localhost' '# added for local testing' '10.0.1.25   todo.local api.todo.local' '10.0.1.30   db.todo.local' > hosts.copy
printf '%s\n' '# Generated by NetworkManager' 'search corp.example.com' 'nameserver 10.0.0.2' 'nameserver 1.1.1.1' 'options timeout:2 attempts:2' > resolv.copy

printf '%s\n' '#!/bin/bash' '# Wait until http://127.0.0.1:8086/health.json answers with a 2xx code.' '# Try 5 times, 1 second apart. Exit 0 when healthy, exit 1 if it never gets healthy.' 'URL=http://127.0.0.1:8086/health.json' 'for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do' '  if curl -s $URL > /dev/null; then' '    echo "healthy after $i tries"' '    exit 0' '  fi' 'done' 'echo "not healthy"' > wait-health.sh

warmup.q: `df` says the disk is full but `du` finds little. What is a common reason?
warmup.a: A process still has a deleted file open. Find it with `lsof +L1` and restart the process (or truncate the file).

warmup.q: Which `free -m` column shows if the server is short of memory?
Which command checks a systemd unit file without installing it?
How do you stop a process politely, then by force?
warmup.a: `kill PID` (SIGTERM) first; `kill -9 PID` (SIGKILL) only if it is still running.

problems.title: Is the app listening and answering? ss + curl
problems.situation: The frontend pod says "backend unavailable". The first two questions are always: does something listen on the port, and does it answer correctly? The user starts a small test server on port 8081 and checks it with `ss` and `curl`.
task: Start a test server in the background: `python3 -m http.server 8081 --bind 127.0.0.1 --directory site > server.log 2>&1 &`.
Show listening TCP sockets on port 8081 with `ss -ltn 'sport = :8081'`.
Get the body of `/health.json` with `curl -s`.
Show only the status line and the Content-Type header (`curl -sI`).
Print only the status code and the size with `curl -s -o /dev/null -w`. Stop the server at the end.
hints: `ss -l` listening, `-t` TCP, `-n` numbers (no names), `-p` process (needs sudo for other users' processes).
`curl -I` = HEAD request, only headers. `-s` = silent (no progress bar).
`-w '%{http_code}\n'` prints the status code after the request.

explanation.meaning: A tiny web server for tests. `--bind 127.0.0.1` = only this machine can reach it.
Show listening TCP sockets with source port 8081. `0.0.0.0` would mean all network interfaces.
Get the body quietly.
Only the response headers: status line, Content-Type, Server ...
Throw the body away and print chosen values. Good for scripts.

problems.expected_output:
State    Recv-Q   Send-Q     Local Address:Port     Peer Address:Port  Process
LISTEN   0        5              127.0.0.1:8081          0.0.0.0:*
{"status":"UP"}
HTTP/1.0 200 OK
Content-type: application/json
status=200 size=16 bytes
mistakes: Using `netstat`: it is old and often not installed. `ss` is the modern replacement (`netstat -tulpn` = `ss -tulpn`).
Server bound to `127.0.0.1` inside a container: other pods cannot reach it. Bind to `0.0.0.0` in containers.
Forgetting `-s`: curl prints a progress table into the script output.
problems.interview_say: I check two things: is something listening, with `ss -tulpn | grep PORT`, and does it answer, with `curl -sI` or `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'`.
problems.try_yourself: Run `ss -tulpn` (as your user, then with sudo). Which ports are open on your WSL?

problems.title: Fix "Address already in use"
problems.situation: After a deploy, the Spring Boot backend does not start: `Port 8082 was already in use`. An old copy of the app was never stopped. The user reproduces the problem with two test servers, finds who holds the port, stops it, and starts again.
task: Start the "old" server on port 8082 in the background.
Start a second one on the same port in the foreground. Read the last line of the error.
Find the PID that holds the port with `lsof -t -i :8082` (or `ss -ltnp`). Show its command with `ps`.
Stop it, start the new server, and check with `curl` that it answers.
hints: Only one process can listen on one IP and port at a time.
`lsof -t -i :PORT` prints only the PID(s).
`fuser 8082/tcp` is another way to find the PID.
solution: python3 -m http.server 8082 --bind 127.0.0.1 > old.log 2>&1 &      # an old copy that was never stopped
python3 -m http.server 8082 --bind 127.0.0.1 2>&1 | tail -n 1       # the new start fails

explanation.meaning: The operating system refuses a second listener on the same address and port.
PIDs of processes using port 8082.
What exactly is it? Check before killing it: it could be another team's service.
Stop the old copy cleanly (SIGTERM), then start the new one.

problems.expected_output:
OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use
port 8082 is held by: python3 -m http.server 8082 --bind 127.0.0.1
new server answers: 200
mistakes: Changing the app to another port to "fix" it. The old process still runs and uses memory; find and stop it.
`kill -9` at once: the old app may not release resources cleanly. Use SIGTERM first.
`lsof -i :8082` shows nothing for processes of other users without `sudo`.
problems.interview_say: For "port already in use" I find the process with `ss -ltnp | grep :PORT` or `lsof -i :PORT`, check what it is with `ps`, stop it cleanly, and then start the new service.
problems.try_yourself: Start the server on `0.0.0.0` and another one on `127.0.0.1`, both on port 8090. Does the second one start? (Try it and read the error.)

problems.title: curl in scripts: -f, timeouts and exit codes
problems.situation: A health-check script must tell the difference between "server answers with an error", "nothing listens on the port" and "server hangs". curl's exit codes say exactly what went wrong, but only with the right options.
task: Start a server on 8083. Request `/missing`: print the status code. What is curl's exit code?
Request `/missing` again with `-f`. What is the exit code now?
Request a closed port (8099). Print the exit code.
Start `nc -l 127.0.0.1 8084` (accepts but never answers). Request it with `--max-time 1`. Print the exit code.
Show the important lines of `curl -v` for `/health.json`.
hints: Without `-f`, an HTTP 404 or 500 is still a "successful" transfer: exit code 0.
Exit codes: 6 could not resolve host, 7 could not connect, 22 HTTP error (with -f), 28 timeout.
`curl -v` writes details to stderr: `2>&1 | grep -E '^(\* Connected|> GET|< HTTP)'`.
solution: curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8099/; echo "closed port, exit code: $?"
curl -s --max-time 1 http://127.0.0.1:8084/; echo "server hangs, exit code: $?"
curl -sv http://127.0.0.1:8083/health.json 2>&1 | grep -E '^(\* Connected|> GET|< HTTP)'

explanation.meaning: Without `-f`, curl only reports transfer problems, not HTTP errors.
HTTP status 400 or more gives exit code 22. Use it in scripts.
Could not connect: nothing listens, or a firewall rejects.
Give up after 1 second. Without a timeout a script can wait for minutes.
Verbose: `*` info, `>` request lines sent, `<` response lines received.
netcat listens and accepts, but never sends an HTTP answer: a hanging server.

problems.expected_output:
status 404, exit code: 0
with -f, exit code: 22
closed port, exit code: 7
server hangs, exit code: 28
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 8083
> GET /health.json HTTP/1.1
< HTTP/1.0 200 OK
problems.output_note: On Ubuntu 22.04 (curl 7.81) the `Connected to` line ends with `(#0)`.
mistakes: Health checks with `curl -s URL && echo ok`: a 500 error page still prints "ok". Add `-f`.
No timeout in cron or CI: the job hangs on a dead server. Always add `--max-time` (or `--connect-timeout`).
problems.interview_say: In scripts I use `curl -fsS --max-time 5 URL`. `-f` turns HTTP errors into a non-zero exit code, and the exit code tells me if it was DNS (6), connect (7), HTTP (22) or timeout (28).
problems.try_yourself: Run `curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{time_total}\n' URL` against the test server. How long did the request take?

problems.title: Name resolution: /etc/hosts, resolv.conf, getent
problems.situation: The backend cannot reach `db.todo.local`. Before blaming the network, the user checks how Linux turns names into IP addresses: first `/etc/hosts`, then the DNS servers in `/etc/resolv.conf`. Practice copies are used so nothing on the system changes.
task: Resolve `localhost` the way programs do: `getent hosts localhost`.
In `hosts.copy`, find the IP for `db.todo.local` and the line for `api.todo.local`.
In `resolv.copy`, list the DNS servers and the search domain.
Try to resolve the unknown name `todo.internal` with `getent` and with `curl`. Print the exit codes.
hints: `getent hosts NAME` uses the same order as programs (see `/etc/nsswitch.conf`: files, then dns).
A hosts line: IP, then one or more names.
`awk '/^nameserver/ {print $2}' resolv.copy`
solution: getent hosts todo.internal || echo "getent: todo.internal not found (exit code $?)"
curl -s --max-time 5 http://todo.internal/; echo "curl exit code: $? (6 = could not resolve host)"

explanation.meaning: Ask the system resolver (hosts file + DNS). Exit code 2 = not found.
Static name list, checked first. Good for tests; dangerous if forgotten on servers.
Which DNS servers to ask (`nameserver`) and which domain to try (`search`). On WSL it is generated.
Could not resolve the host: a name problem, not a network or app problem.

problems.expected_output:
127.0.0.1       localhost
db.todo.local -> 10.0.1.30
10.0.1.25   todo.local api.todo.local
search domain: corp.example.com
DNS server: 10.0.0.2
DNS server: 1.1.1.1
getent: todo.internal not found (exit code 2)
curl exit code: 6 (6 = could not resolve host)
mistakes: Testing with `ping name` only: ping uses the same resolver, but a blocked ICMP looks like a DNS problem.
An old line in `/etc/hosts` that points a name to a dead server. `dig` shows the right IP, but programs still use the hosts file.
problems.interview_say: Linux resolves names first from `/etc/hosts`, then from the DNS servers in `/etc/resolv.conf`. I compare `getent hosts name` with `dig name` to see if the hosts file or DNS gives a wrong answer.
problems.try_yourself: Run `cat /etc/resolv.conf` on your WSL (read only). Which nameserver does WSL use?

problems.title: Find the bug: the wait-for-health script
problems.situation: The deploy pipeline runs `wait-health.sh` after starting the backend. It said "healthy" even though the app returned 404, and when the app is down it finishes at once and still exits with 0, so the pipeline continues.
task: Start a server on 8086 that serves the empty folder `app5` (so `/health.json` is 404). Run `bash wait-health.sh; echo $?`.
Find 4 bugs: no `-f`, no sleep between tries, no timeout, and the wrong final exit code.
Fix the script. Run it again: it must try 5 times and exit 1.
Create `app5/health.json` and run it again: it must say healthy and exit 0.
hints: `curl -s` returns 0 for a 404 page. Use `curl -fsS --max-time 2`.
Add `sleep 1` after a failed try.
End with `exit 1` after the loop.
solution: # Wait until http://127.0.0.1:8086/health.json answers with a 2xx code.
# Try 5 times, 1 second apart. Exit 0 when healthy, exit 1 if it never gets healthy.

explanation.meaning: Bug 1: without it, the 404 page counted as healthy.
Bug 2: 5 tries in a few milliseconds give a slow app no time to start.
Bug 3: a hanging app would block the pipeline.
Bug 4: the script ended with `echo`, so the exit code was 0 and the pipeline went on.
Quote variables, as always.

problems.expected_output:
healthy after 1 tries
exit code: 0
--- fixed, app returns 404 ---
try 1: not healthy yet
try 2: not healthy yet
try 3: not healthy yet
try 4: not healthy yet
try 5: not healthy yet
not healthy after 5 tries
exit code: 1
--- fixed, app is healthy ---
healthy after 1 tries
exit code: 0
mistakes: Checking only that the port is open (`nc -z`). The app can listen and still answer 500. Check the health endpoint.
Retrying forever. A deploy step needs a clear limit and a non-zero exit code.
problems.interview_say: My wait-for-health loop uses `curl -fsS --max-time`, sleeps between tries, stops after a limit, and exits 1 so the pipeline stops and can roll back.
problems.try_yourself: Make the URL and the number of tries arguments with defaults: `URL=${1:-http://127.0.0.1:8086/health.json}` and `TRIES=${2:-5}`.

problems.title: Know your machine: ip a, ip r, ping
problems.situation: A new teammate asks: "What is the IP of your WSL machine, and where does its traffic go?" The user shows the network interfaces, the routing table and a ping test.
task: Show the interfaces and IP addresses in short form: `ip -br a`.
Show the routing table: `ip r`. Find the `default via` line.
Ping the loopback address 2 times: `ping -c 2 127.0.0.1`.
hints: `lo` is the loopback interface (127.0.0.1). `eth0` is the main network card in WSL.
The default route is the gateway for all other networks.
`-c 2` = send only 2 packets. Without `-c`, ping runs until Ctrl+C.

explanation.meaning: Brief list of interfaces: name, state (UP/DOWN), addresses with prefix (`/24`).
Routes. `default via X` = gateway; other lines = directly connected networks.
Send 2 ICMP echo requests; shows packet loss and round-trip time.
Old tools (package net-tools). `ip` replaces them.

problems.expected_output:
lo               UNKNOWN        127.0.0.1/8
ifb0             DOWN
ifb1             DOWN
eth0             UP             192.0.2.2/24
default via 192.0.2.1 dev eth0
192.0.2.0/24 dev eth0 proto kernel scope link src 192.0.2.2
2 packets transmitted, 2 received, 0% packet loss, time 1004ms
rtt min/avg/max/mdev = 0.027/0.030/0.034/0.003 ms
problems.output_note: Interface names, IP addresses and times are different on every machine.
mistakes: "Ping fails, so the server is down." Many cloud servers block ICMP. Test the real port with `nc -zv host 443` or `curl`.
Reading `/24` as a host number. It is the prefix length: 24 bits for the network (255.255.255.0).
problems.interview_say: `ip a` shows my interfaces and addresses, `ip r` shows the routes and the default gateway. Ping only tests ICMP, so to test a service I use the real port with `nc -zv` or `curl`.
problems.try_yourself: Run `ip -4 -o a | awk '{print $2, $4}'` to print only interface names and IPv4 addresses.

problems.title: dig, nslookup, nc and traceroute (needs internet)
problems.situation: These tools talk to the real internet, so they are not run in the sandbox. On WSL with internet, the user checks a DNS record, tests a remote port, and sees the path packets take.
task: Install the tools if needed: `sudo apt install -y dnsutils traceroute netcat-openbsd`.
Ask DNS for github.com: `dig +short github.com` and `nslookup github.com`.
Test if port 443 is open: `nc -zv -w 3 github.com 443`.
Show the route: `traceroute -n -m 8 github.com`.
hints: `dig +short` prints only the answer (IP addresses).
`nc -z` = only test the connection, send nothing. `-w 3` = 3 second timeout.
Stars `* * *` in traceroute = a router that does not answer traceroute packets (often normal).

explanation.meaning: DNS query, short answer. Without `+short`: question, answer, TTL and the server that answered.
Simple DNS lookup; shows which server answered.
Port test: `succeeded` = open; `refused` = closed; timeout = filtered by a firewall.
Show up to 8 hops (routers) with numbers only.

problems.output_note: IP addresses, DNS servers and times depend on the user's network and location.
problems.typical_output:
20.205.243.166
Server:		10.255.255.254
Address:	10.255.255.254#53

Non-authoritative answer:
Name:	github.com
Address: 20.205.243.166

Connection to github.com (20.205.243.166) 443 port [tcp/https] succeeded!
traceroute to github.com (20.205.243.166), 8 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  172.24.208.1  0.412 ms  0.370 ms  0.361 ms
 2  192.168.1.1  2.115 ms  2.087 ms  2.071 ms

mistakes: `nc: getaddrinfo for host "github.co" port 443: Name or service not known` means a DNS (name) problem, not a closed port.
problems.interview_say: I use `dig` to check DNS answers, `nc -zv host port` to test if a TCP port is reachable, and `traceroute` to see where packets stop.
problems.try_yourself: Run `dig github.com MX` and `dig github.com TXT`. What other record types do you know?

interview.q: How do you check which ports are open and which process uses them?
interview.a: `sudo ss -tulpn` (TCP and UDP, listening, numbers, process). The old command is `netstat -tulpn`.

interview.q: How do you fix "port already in use"?
interview.a: Find the process with `ss -ltnp | grep :PORT` or `lsof -i :PORT`, check what it is with `ps`, stop it cleanly, then start the new service.

interview.q: What curl options do you use in a health-check script?
interview.a: `curl -fsS --max-time 5 URL`: `-f` fails on HTTP errors, `-s` silent, `-S` still show errors, and a timeout so the script never hangs.

interview.q: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
interview.a: TCP is connection-based and reliable (HTTP, SSH, databases). UDP has no connection and no delivery guarantee, but is fast (DNS queries, video, metrics).

interview.q: How does Linux resolve a host name?
interview.a: First `/etc/hosts`, then the DNS servers in `/etc/resolv.conf` (the order is set in `/etc/nsswitch.conf`). `getent hosts name` shows the result programs get.
